title: Study
description: Spoken chapters from my study texts, starting with The Practical Historian.
author: Study

episodes.title: The Practical Historian 1: The Epistemological Foundation
episodes.description: Source versus evidence, witting and unwitting testimony, independence, the argument from silence, and what proof means in history.

episodes.title: The Practical Historian 2: Primary Source Analysis by Type
episodes.description: Reading the diplomatic, official, press, memoir, diary and visual genres against the grain.

episodes.title: The Practical Historian 3: Quantitative Methods and Their Limits
episodes.description: What data is as a source, and what quantitative instincts must be unlearned in the archive.

episodes.title: The Practical Historian 4: Essay and Argument Construction
episodes.description: Thesis, warrant, the paragraph as a move, counterevidence, and the uses of quotation.

episodes.title: The Practical Historian 5: Writing, Style, and the Form of Historical Prose
episodes.description: Prose choices as analytical choices: agency, modality, and the inherited vocabulary.

episodes.title: The Practical Historian 6: Working with Historiography
episodes.description: Reading secondary work as argument, mapping a debate, and positioning a contribution.

episodes.title: The Practical Historian 7: Forms of Output: Genre, Constraint, and Assessment
episodes.description: What each kind of deliverable is for, what makes it good, and how it is judged, including the abstract.

episodes.title: The Practical Historian 8: Research Workflow, with the Coda
episodes.description: The system that performs all of the above at scale: notes, tools, backup, and the use of IT and AI.
